 K_Y+\Delta\sim_{\mathbb Q}f^*L,\qquad L\in\mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}(X)_{\mathbb Q}.$$
Fix a model $f':(Y',\Delta')\to X'$ as in [eq:moduli] and a prime $P\subset X'$.

Over $U$, the map and the boundary strata are smooth, the boundary is relatively SNC with coefficients in $[0,1]$, and $$\mathcal G_m
 =p_*\mathcal O_W\bigl(m(K_{W/S}+D_W)\bigr)|_U
 \simeq \mathcal O_S(mQ_S)|_U.$$

Let a real-polarizable variation of pure Hodge structure be given on the complement of an SNC divisor in a polydisk, with quasi-unipotent local monodromies.*

On a dense open $P^\circ$ mapping into $U$, suppose a connected fiber component $A_x^*$ of the deepest stratum has been selected in family.
We retain the good open $U$, the log-smooth family, and the integer $m$ of the preceding sections.

Let $(F,D)$ be a smooth connected compact Kähler pair, with effective SNC rational boundary of coefficients less than one, and suppose that $m(K_F+D)$ is trivial.
Let $g:E^\circ\to B^\circ$ be a proper smooth holomorphic map of connected complex manifolds, with connected compact fibers and a section.

evidence.quote: In the setup of [orders:adjoint], choose locally a frame $s$ of $\mathcal O_S(mQ_S)$, and let $\tau$ be its tautological root as in Section 3.1. For every prime $P\subset S$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{ord}}_P^{\mathrm{Hdg}}(\tau)=t_P-1. \label{orders:traceorder}$$* *More precisely, let $\pi:\widetilde V\to V$ be a coordinate power chart making the local pure variation unipotent, and let $\overline{\mathcal E}_\chi$ be its extended highest eigenline. For a sufficiently divisible positive integer $a$, the open identification $s^{\otimes a}\leftrightarrow \tau^{\otimes am}$ extends to an isomorphism of actual bundles $$\pi^*\mathcal O_S(amM_S)|_{\widetilde V} \simeq \overline{\mathcal E}_\chi^{\otimes am}. \label{orders:tracebundle}$$ One integer $a$ suffices on the compact base. The resulting extension rule commutes with pullback to disks generically meeting $U$, after further power substitution on the disk. All assertions allow arbitrary rational coefficients on the vertical components of $D_W$.

outputs.exact_statement:
Under the assumptions above, $\mathbf M$ is b-semiample. More explicitly, there is a smooth compact Kähler modification $\mu_0:S\to X$ such that:*

1.  *for every smooth compact Kähler modification $\nu:S_1\to S$, $$M_{S_1}=\nu^*M_S\quad\text{in }\mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}(S_1)_{\mathbb Q};$$*

2.  *for some positive integer $m$, the actual line bundle representing $mM_S$ is generated by its global holomorphic sections.*

*The theorem includes a point base and relative dimension zero. No projectivity of $f$, $X$, or $Y$ is assumed.

Fix a model $f':(Y',\Delta')\to X'$ as in [eq:moduli] and a prime $P\subset X'$. On a joint log resolution of $\Delta'$ and $(f')^*P$, let $\delta_E$ be the crepant coefficient and $a_E=\mathop{\mathrm{ord}}_E((f')^*P)>0$. Over a general point of $P$, $$t_P=\min_{E\mapsto P}\frac{1-\delta_E}{a_E}.$$ In particular, the threshold is rational and unchanged by a further resolution of the source. The divisor $B_{X'}$ has finite support.

Over $V^\circ$, the form $\tau$ is a relative top form with at most logarithmic poles on $H$ and no other poles. At a strict covering prime over a horizontal divisor of coefficient $\delta$, if $j$ is the ramification index, its order is $$j(1-\delta)-1.$$

Let a real-polarizable variation of pure Hodge structure be given on the complement of an SNC divisor in a polydisk, with quasi-unipotent local monodromies.* 1. *After coordinate power substitutions making all local monodromies unipotent, its Hodge filtrations extend by subbundles of the canonical flat bundle. On a disk, the filtration also extends by subbundles of either the upper or the lower canonical bundle before unipotentization.* 2. *After coordinate power substitutions making the monodromies unipotent, the canonical extension and its Hodge filtration commute with further powers and with pullback to any disk whose punctured image lies in the given open.* 3. *A real pure Hodge morphism has flat Hodge kernels and images, with flat Hodge complements. Its split maps and finite-group eigenspace projectors are compatible with the canonical extensions in (i). After unipotentization, tensor constructions are compatible as well.* 4. *On a unipotent disk, a nonvanishing frame $e$ of an extended highest Hodge line satisfies, for some constants $C,A>0$, $$C^{-1}(1+|\log|t||)^{-A} \leq \|e(t)\| \leq C(1+|\log|t||)^A. \label{hodge:logbounds}$$ The constants may depend on the disk. The same assertion applies to Hodge determinant lines.

Let a mixed variation on a punctured disk be extended in its upper canonical flat bundle, with the canonical weight filtration and locally free double Hodge/weight grades, as in [hodge:FF]. Suppose a finite-group character summand satisfies $$\dim F^d=1,\qquad F^{d+1}=0,$$ and the sole nonzero $F^d$ weight grade has weight $w$. Then projection to $\mathop{\mathrm{Gr}}^W_w$ identifies the extended top line with the canonically extended top line of that pure grade.

Let $k$ be the maximal number of horizontal coefficient-one components meeting in a good fiber, constant after shrinking $U$. For the local root family above:* 1. *$$F^d\mathbb V_\chi=\mathcal O_{V^\circ}\tau.$$ This line lies in the single pure weight grade $\mathop{\mathrm{Gr}}^W_{d+k}\mathbb V_\chi$.* 2. *Choose a depth-$k$ intersection component downstairs dominating the good open. After a good-open base change selecting one connected component $A_x^*$ of its fibers, take every root-cover sheet above that component. Iterated residue identifies the line in (i), through its pure grade and with the Tate twist removed, with the highest eigenline of the resolved root cover of the induced klt volume on $A_x^*$. In degree $m$ this is the specified plurivolume identification from SNC adjunction.* 3. *These highest-line identifications preserve generators in canonical extensions on unipotent disks. In a disk model satisfying the hypotheses of [hodge:FF], its extended mixed top line projects isomorphically to the same pure line.* *If $k=0$, the intersection is the whole original fiber, there is no removed divisor, and the pure root-cover cohomology itself provides the line.

Over a smooth good open, let $\varphi:(Z',H')\to(Z,H)$ be a proper equivariant modification between smooth families of SNC pairs, with $H'$ the reduced inverse image of $H$. Pullback is an isomorphism on top logarithmic-form spaces. In the character summand of Proposition 7, it identifies the top line and the top line of its unique pure weight grade.* *Suppose further that, over a disk, the new compactification satisfies the hypotheses of [hodge:FF]. If the original variation has been made unipotent, testing extension of the pulled-back volume in $g'_*\omega_{Z'/\Delta}(H')$ tests the canonical extension of the original top line. It is not necessary to assume unipotence of every summand newly appearing in the cohomology of $Z'\setminus H'$.

Fix a prime divisor $P\subset S$. On a resolution over a general point of $P$, arrange joint SNC support for the crepant divisor and $p^*P$. Write $\delta_E$ for the crepant coefficient and $a_E=\mathop{\mathrm{ord}}_E(p^*P)>0$ for the components dominating $P$. Then $$t_P=\min_{E\mapsto P}\frac{1-\delta_E}{a_E}.
 \label{orders:thresholdformula}$$ This minimum computes the threshold over all divisorial valuations, including valuations exceptional over the chosen resolution.

Fix the local root family of Section 3.1 and a resolved transverse disk downstairs. For every sufficiently divisible power substitution $t=u^N$, there is a smooth equivariant Kähler model over $\Delta_u$ with the following properties:* 1. *It retains every component of the generic root cover and maps to the downstairs order resolution. On the punctured disk it is a modification of the pulled-back root family.* 2. *The horizontal removed divisor $H_N$, defined by the reduced full inverse image of the original removed divisor on the punctured disk and then closed up, is SNC. Its support and the full central fiber have joint SNC support.* 3. *Every stratum of $(Z_N,H_N)$ dominates the disk and is smooth over a smaller punctured disk.* 4. *For each vertical prime $E$ on the downstairs order resolution, some prime on $Z_N$ dominates $E$.* *Consequently [hodge:FF] applies to this model, and its top eigenline tests the extension of the original line as in Lemma 8.

The section $\tau$ is meromorphic in that extended line. Its normalized order is $$\mathop{\mathrm{ord}}^{\mathrm{Hdg}}_0(\tau)
       =\min_E\frac{l_E+1-a_E}{a_E},
 \label{orders:generalorder}$$ where $E$ runs through the central-fiber primes on the downstairs resolution. The normalization divides an ordinary order after $t=u^N$ by $N$. At the displayed order, the corrected section generates the extension after clearing its denominator.

In the setup of [orders:adjoint], choose locally a frame $s$ of $\mathcal O_S(mQ_S)$, and let $\tau$ be its tautological root as in Section 3.1. For every prime $P\subset S$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{ord}}_P^{\mathrm{Hdg}}(\tau)=t_P-1. \label{orders:traceorder}$$* *More precisely, let $\pi:\widetilde V\to V$ be a coordinate power chart making the local pure variation unipotent, and let $\overline{\mathcal E}_\chi$ be its extended highest eigenline. For a sufficiently divisible positive integer $a$, the open identification $s^{\otimes a}\leftrightarrow \tau^{\otimes am}$ extends to an isomorphism of actual bundles $$\pi^*\mathcal O_S(amM_S)|_{\widetilde V} \simeq \overline{\mathcal E}_\chi^{\otimes am}. \label{orders:tracebundle}$$ One integer $a$ suffices on the compact base. The resulting extension rule commutes with pullback to disks generically meeting $U$, after further power substitution on the disk. All assertions allow arbitrary rational coefficients on the vertical components of $D_W$.

For the original fibration and the smooth compact Kähler model $S$ fixed above, every smooth compact Kähler modification $
u:S_1	o S$ satisfies $$M_{S_1}=
u^*M_S
                         \quad	ext{in }\mathop{\mathrm{Pic}}(S_1)\otimes\mathbb Q.$$ No assumption that $
u$ be an isomorphism over $U$ is needed.

The expression [orders:residuenormformula] is a positive finite norm, homogeneous of degree one, on the volume line. Let $a$ clear the indicated powers. Along any disk in $P$ whose punctured part lies in $P^\circ$, after a sufficiently divisible power substitution, a nonvanishing local frame of $$r^*\mathcal O_S(amM_S)$$ and its dual have at most powers-of-log growth in the $a$-th tensor power of this norm and its dual norm. No Kähler assumption on $P$ is required.

There are a smooth compact Kähler manifold $\Sigma$, a proper surjection $\rho:\Sigma\to S$, and a dense open $\Sigma^\circ\subseteq\rho^{-1}(U)$ with the following data:*

1.  *a proper smooth family $a:\mathscr A^\circ\to\Sigma^\circ$ with connected fibers and a holomorphic section;*

2.  *an effective relative SNC rational boundary $D_{\mathscr A}$ with coefficients in $[0,1)$;*

3.  *an identification $$a_*\mathcal O_{\mathscr A^\circ}
           \bigl(m(K_{\mathscr A^\circ/\Sigma^\circ}+D_{\mathscr A})\bigr)
     \simeq \rho^*\mathcal G_m.$$ The relative log-pluri bundle itself is the pullback of this line. Moreover, $\mathscr A^\circ$ and its boundary have extensions in a smooth compact Kähler manifold mapping to $\Sigma$.*

*Each fiber pair is a connected component of a deepest coefficient-one stratum of the original good family, with its adjunction boundary.

Let $P$ be a smooth compact complex manifold and $r:P\to S$ a holomorphic map factoring through the marked-family construction on a dense open $P^\circ$. Equip $r^*\mathcal G_m$ there with [spread:residue-norm]. Along a disk in $P$ mapping generically to $P^\circ$, generators of any sufficiently divisible positive power of $r^*(mM_S)$, and the dual generators, have at most powers-of-logarithm growth in the corresponding norms, after a sufficiently divisible power substitution.

Let $(F,D)$ be a smooth connected compact Kähler pair, with effective SNC rational boundary of coefficients less than one, and suppose that $m(K_F+D)$ is trivial. There is a finite étale cover $\nu:J\to F$ and an isomorphism of pairs $$\label{spread:fiber-product}
 (J,\nu^*D)\simeq (Q,C)\times T_1\times\cdots\times T_j,$$ where $(Q,C)$ is a smooth projective klt SNC pair, and each $T_i$ is a positive-dimensional complex torus or an irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifold. The boundary is entirely on $Q$. A point is allowed for $Q$, and $j=0$ is allowed. Moreover, $m(K_Q+C)$ and all $mK_{T_i}$ are trivial.

Let $g:E^\circ\to B^\circ$ be a proper smooth holomorphic map of connected complex manifolds, with connected compact fibers and a section. Suppose $B^\circ$ is a dense open in a smooth compact Kähler manifold $B$, and the family has a smooth compact Kähler extension $E\to B$. Then all finite connected étale covers of individual fibers occur in countably many families, each obtained after a finite étale base cover of $B^\circ$. Each resulting base and total space admit smooth compact Kähler extensions preserving the open families. The same holds with pulled-back relative SNC boundary data.

Let $q:Z\to T$ be a proper holomorphic map of compact complex spaces. The image of a constructible subset of $Z$ is constructible in $T$. Consequently, any finite combination of incidence, emptiness, surjectivity, and injectivity conditions on fibers of compact analytic diagrams is constructible.

Let $(\mathbb V_{\mathbb Z},F^\bullet)$ be an integral pure variation with a flat real polarization $B$. There is a flat real automorphism $C$ of $\mathbb V_{\mathbb R}$ such that $(\mathbb V_{\mathbb Z},C^{-1}F^\bullet)$ is polarized by a rational form $B'$, and $$B'(x,y)=B(Cx,Cy).$$ Consequently the new and original variations are isomorphic as real polarized variations, and their holomorphic Hodge bundles are isomorphic. Their canonical Hodge extensions are also identified wherever local monodromy is unipotent. After multiplying $B'$ by a positive integer, its values on $\mathbb V_{\mathbb Z}$ are integral.

Let $B$ be a smooth compact complex manifold, let $D$ be an SNC divisor, and let $\mathbb V$ be a real-polarizable integral variation on $B^\circ=B\setminus D$. Suppose its Hodge numbers are either $$w=1,\quad h^{1,0}=h^{0,1}=g,
  \qquad\text{or}\qquad
  w=2,\quad h^{2,0}=h^{0,2}=1.$$ After a finite cover of $B^\circ$, extended and resolved over $B$, the canonical extension of its Griffiths line is semiample. The resulting base is smooth and compact and its boundary can be taken SNC.

Let $r:P\to S$ and the smooth families $t_i:T_i\to P^\circ$ be as in Proposition 20, with $n_i=\dim T_{i,u}>0$, and put $$\mathcal H_i=F^{n_i}\bigl(R^{n_i}(t_i)_*\mathbb C\otimes\mathcal O_{P^\circ}\bigr).$$ Thus $\mathcal H_i$ is the highest line denoted $\lambda_i$ in Proposition 20; the symbol $\lambda$ above denotes the Griffiths line. After a proper generically finite surjection $\pi:P'\to P$, obtained by extending a finite *étale* cover of the good open and resolving, there are semiample holomorphic line bundles $\overline{\mathcal H}_i$ on the smooth compact manifold $P'$ whose specified restrictions are $\pi^*\mathcal H_i$.* *The boundary may be taken SNC. Along any disk in $P'$ whose punctured disk lies in the good open, a generator of $\overline{\mathcal H}_i$ and its inverse have at most powers-of-logarithm growth in the volume norm [periods:volume] and its dual. The same is true for all positive powers, including the powers used in the product-volume identification of Proposition 20.

Let $P$ be a complex manifold, $D$ a simple normal crossing divisor, and $P^\circ=P\setminus D$. Let $E_1,E_2$ be holomorphic line bundles on $P$, equipped on $P^\circ$ with Hermitian norms, and let $$\phi:E_1|_{P^\circ}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }E_2|_{P^\circ}$$ be a specified holomorphic isomorphism. Assume the following near the smooth locus of each component of $D$. In a coordinate polydisk $(t,z)$ with $D=(t=0)$, choose nonvanishing holomorphic frames $e_1,e_2$. For a dense set of centers $z$, their norms and dual norms along the parallel punctured disks satisfy bounds by powers of $1+|\log|t||$. The constants and powers may depend on the disk. Assume also that $\phi$ compares the two norms by factors bounded above and below on each such disk. It is enough for these bounds to hold after a finite power substitution on each disk. Then $\phi$ extends uniquely to a holomorphic isomorphism $E_1\simeq E_2$ on $P$.

Let $r:P\to S$ be a proper surjective holomorphic map of connected compact complex manifolds, and let $A$ be a holomorphic line bundle on $S$. If $r^*A$ is semiample, then $A$ is semiample. More precisely, let $$P\xrightarrow{h}T\xrightarrow{q}S$$ be the Stein factorization, and let $d$ be the generic degree of $q$. If $r^*(A^{\otimes n})$ is globally generated, then $A^{\otimes nd}$ is globally generated. The same descent conclusion holds for rational holomorphic line bundles after clearing denominators.

purpose: B-semiampleness for compact log-smooth Kähler fibrations

coverage.checked_domain: All ordered singleton and pair inputs from delta in {-1,0,1/2,1,3/2} and multiplicity in {1,2}; ties, negative thresholds, repeated rows, malformed inputs, size boundaries and large integers.
coverage.oracle_basis: Exact integer SNC inequalities, with an equality witness for the supplied minimum; the existence and completeness of the geometric resolution remain preconditions.

coverage.checked_domain: The rational arithmetic shift threshold minus one on the same finite vectors.
coverage.oracle_basis: Independent Fraction arithmetic checks the shift; canonical Hodge extension and geometric order identification are not executed.

title: B-semiampleness for compact log-smooth Kähler fibrations
